config.py:173-178: mode=before validator raises ValueError(TEMPERATURE_REMOVED_MESSAGE) when data is a dict containing 'temperature'. Pydantic wraps it in ValidationError (msg 'Value error, <text>'). Config.load (config.py:850-860) re-raises it unchanged (only BOM files become ConfigBomError). cli.py serve (203-207) and validate (259-262) catch Exception, print _format_config_error(e), and raise typer.Exit(code=2). _format_config_error (cli.py:103-104) uses validation_error_lines (_errors.py:16-25), which emits loc and msg and so includes the message text. Both inputs reach the validator as a dict. TOML [llm] is a dict. Env SQLLENS_LLM__TEMPERATURE reaches it through env_nested_delimiter='__' (config.py:770), which nests it as llm={'temperature': ...}. I did not read the pydantic-settings source (no dependency_sources were supplied), so the env nesting of an undeclared nested key rests on that setting plus the repo tests test_validate_rejects_env_temperature and test_serve_rejects_toml_temperature_before_starting in tests/unit/test_llm_sampling_options.py:219-234. I did not run those tests.

LLMConfig (config.py:139-178) is a plain BaseModel with no model_config, so pydantic's default extra='ignore' applies; the other nested models set extra='forbid' explicitly (e.g. lines 287, 307, 459, 494), and the comment at 285-287 and 491 notes the top-level Config's forbid does not reach nested models. So an unknown key such as temperature under [llm] would be dropped silently without the before-validator _reject_temperature (173-178). Input traced: {'temperature': 0.5} passed to LLMConfig; with no validator it is ignored, with the validator it raises.

It asserts the captured streams are [False, True], so both send_request and stream_request are covered. It also asserts body['output_config']=={'effort':'high'} and 'temperature' not in body on each body. This is the transport-captured body, not a stubbed messages object. I did not run the tests or read the SDK source, so I did not confirm that the SDK serializes output_config unchanged; the test asserts it on the captured body.

The message (config.py:132-136) names `temperature` and says 'Remove `temperature` from the [llm] section (and unset SQLLENS_LLM__TEMPERATURE)'. With temperature unset, validate reaches console.print('Config OK') (cli.py:272) and exits 0 (test at :238). Other validate exits (loopback policy, cli.py:266-271) -> outside the trigger because they need a different fault and config load already failed first for temperature inputs. Tests cover all five listed inputs plus serve and the unset case. I read the code and tests and did not run pytest.
